before: value is String asks whether the value is a String. Any is a common supertype for non-null Kotlin values.
Within this branch, the compiler knows the stable val value is a String, so length can be used without a manual cast.
A mutable property or a value that may change between checks can prevent the compiler from retaining the proof. Smart casts depend on stability.
A type check does not change the object into another type. A non-String follows the else branch.
Expected output or behavior: 4. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Compare a String and an Int in the same checked branch. State which operations are allowed after the proof. You may trace it without a Kotlin compiler; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: `Any` is a type that can hold any non-null Kotlin value. The actual value might be text, a number, or another kind of object.
The check `value is String` asks whether the actual value is text. It does not turn a number into text.
After a successful check, Kotlin lets this branch use the value as a String. This is called a smart cast. Here, it allows access to `length`.
A smart cast needs the checked value to stay reliable. If a property could change before it is used, the compiler may require another check or a stable local value.
The screen shows `4`. The value is the text star, so the String branch reads its length.
If the actual value is not a String, the else branch runs. Only the successful String branch uses the String's length.
